<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par122 />{{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=6}}, fem., ''Judaea''; {{GHGheb|text=אֱדֹם}} masc., ''Idumaei'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=20|verse=20}}; fem., ''Idumaea'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=49|verse=17}}. Nevertheless, it sometimes happens that by a very common transference of thought (just as we say ''Turkey concludes peace'') these names are construed as feminine, even when they denote not the country but the inhabitants; so {{GHGheb|text=יְהוּדָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=3}}; cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=10|verse=7}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=12|verse=33|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=8|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=24|verse=9|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=2}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=2|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=42|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=50|verse=10}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=15}}. Hence the frequent personification of nations (as well as of countries and towns, see ''h'', note 5) as female beings, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=50|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=54|verse=1|hidebook=1}} ff., and the use of the expressions {{GHGheb|text=בַּת בָּבֶל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=1}} ff., {{GHGheb|text=בַּת צִיּוֹן}} &c. (see above) as collective poetical personifications of the people.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|k}}
(''b'') Appellative nouns, which denote a ''circumscribed space'', such as {{GHGheb|text=אֶ֫רֶץ|translate=earth, land}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּבֵל|translate=world}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאֹל|translate=the abode of the dead}}, {{GHGheb|text=כִּכָּר|translate=circle}} (of the Jordan valley), {{GHGheb|text=עִיר|translate=a town}}, {{GHGheb|text=בְּאֵר|translate=a well}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָפוֹן|translate=the north}}, {{GHGheb|text=תֵּימָן|translate=the south}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|l}}
In the majority of nouns denoting place the gender is variable, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫רַח}} and {{GHGheb|text=דֶּ֫רֶךְ|translate=a way}} (usually feminine; the masculine gender only begins to predominate with Ezekiel; cf. Albrecht, l. c., 1896, p. 55), {{GHGheb|text=גַּיְא}} ({{GHGheb|text=גַּי}}) ''valley'', {{GHGheb|text=גַּן|translate=garden}} (fem. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=15}}, unless {{GHGheb|text=לְעָבְדֹה}}, &c., is to be read), {{GHGheb|text=הֵיכָל|translate=palace, temple}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָצֵר|translate=court}}, {{GHGheb|text=כֶּ֫רֶם|translate=vineyard}}, {{GHGheb|text=שַׁ֫עַר|translate=door}},<ref>{{GHGheb|text=מַֽחֲנֶה|translate=camp}} is feminine only when it is a collective, denoting the persons in a camp.</ref> &c.; also {{GHGheb|text=מָקוֹם|translate=place}}, at least in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=18|verse=24}} (referring to Sodom), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=20|verse=9}}, and {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=17|verse=12}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, is construed as feminine. The mountains and hills commanding the surrounding country are almost without exception masculine (see Albrecht, l. c., p. 60 f.).

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|m}}
(''c'') The names of ''instruments, utensils'', and (on the same analogy) ''members'' and ''parts of the body'' in man or beast, since these are all regarded as subservient and subordinate (consequently as feminine).

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|n}}
Thus {{GHGheb|text=חֶ֫רֶב|translate=sword}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָתֵד|translate=tent-peg}}, {{GHGheb|text=כַּד|translate=bucket}}, {{GHGheb|text=כּוֹס|translate=cup}}, {{GHGheb|text=נַ֫עַל|translate=shoe}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫רֶשׂ|translate=bed}}, &c.; in other cases, as {{GHGheb|text=אֲרוֹן|translate=chest, ark}} (with the article {{GHGheb|text=הָֽאָרוֹן}}), {{GHGheb|text=תַּנּוּר|translate=oven}}, the gender is variable. (‘Instruments for binding or holding, girdles and the like, as constraining and mastering, are masculine,’ Albrecht, l. c., p. 89.)—Also {{GHGheb|text=אֹ֫זֶן|translate=ear}} (and in general, members occurring in pairs, Albrecht, l. c., p. 73 f.), {{GHGheb|text=אֶצְבַּע|translate=finger}} (and so probably {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫הֶן|translate=thumb, great toe}}), {{GHGheb|text=יָד}} and {{GHGheb|text=כַּף|translate=hand}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין|translate=right hand}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫גֶל|translate=foot}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫רֶךְ|translate=knee}}, {{GHGheb|text=יָרֵךְ|translate=thigh}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּתֵף|translate=shoulder}}, {{GHGheb|text=לְחִי|translate=cheek}}, {{GHGheb|text=בֶּ֫טֶן|translate=belly}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּנָף|translate=wing}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֶ֫רֶן|translate=horn}}, {{GHGheb|text=שֵׁן|translate=tooth}}; as a rule also {{GHGheb|text=זְרוֹעַ|translate=arm}} (masc. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=5}}, &c.), {{GHGheb|text=לָשׁוֹן|translate=tongue}} (masc. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=22|verse=16}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=28}}, &c.), {{GHGheb|text=עַ֫יִן|translate=eye}} (masc. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=3|verse=9}}, &c.), {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹק|translate=thigh}} (masc. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=29|verse=27}}).<ref>{{GHGheb|text=אַף|translate=nose}}, {{GHGheb|text=גִּיד|translate=sinew}}, {{GHGheb|text=זָנָב|translate=tail}}, {{GHGheb|text=חֵךְ|translate=palate}}, {{GHGheb|text=כָּבֵד|translate=liver}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵב}}, {{GHGheb|text=לֵבָב|translate=heart}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵעִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=רַֽחֲמִים|translate=bowels}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫צַח|translate=forehead}}, {{GHGheb|text=עוֹר|translate=skin}}, {{GHGheb|text=עֹרֶף|translate=back of the neck}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֶּה|translate=mouth}}, {{GHGheb|text=צַוָּאר|translate=neck}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹאשׁ|translate=head}}, {{GHGheb|text=שְׁכֶם|translate=shoulder}}, also {{GHGheb|text=רֶ֫חֶם|translate=womb}}, except in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=20|verse=17}}, are invariably construed as masculine.—{{GHGheb|text=עֶ֫צֶם|translate=bone}} is common.</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|122|o}}
(''d'') Certain names of natural forces or substances are feminine, being probably regarded as instruments, while in the names of the heavens, the heavenly bodies and natural phenomena, the masculine generally predominates (cf. Albrecht, l. c., p. 323 ff.); thus feminine are {{GHGheb|text=שֶׁ֫מֶשׁ|translate=sun}} (but often also {{GHGterm|masc.}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=19|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=104|verse=19|hidebook=1}}); {{GHGheb|text=אֵשׁ}} (Ethiopic ''ʾĕsât'')<section end=par122 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
